leftEvidence.title: A council decides that one man should die

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Chief priests and Pharisees gather a council; Caiaphas argues that one person should die for the people, the narrator widens the statement, and from that day they plan Jesus’ death.
points.right: Paul addresses children of Abraham’s stock and God-fearing hearers in a synagogue setting.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The passage materially bears on the Crucifixion while leaving part of its motive, mechanism, or later significance unstated.
points.right: The same event is narrated as fulfilled Scripture and as a sequence of human and divine actions.

payload.posture: A council’s decision that one man should die can be inspected beside Paul’s later account of rulers, condemnation, tree, tomb, raising, and forgiveness.

rightEvidence.role: The event named in public proclamation
rightEvidence.title: Condemned, taken from the tree, laid in a tomb, and proclaimed

payload.tension: John attributes an unintended wider statement to the high priest; Acts presents a retrospective proclamation to a synagogue audience.
payload.title: One should die / death publicly recounted
